text:
Marathon Petroleum rose a modest 0.24% today, but that's really the tail end of a sharp two-week rally up 13.2%. The driver throughout has been crude oil prices: US oil climbed from around $90 to nearly $102 per barrel as Iran escalated attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global oil supply. Refineries like Marathon benefit directly when crude prices rise because they can sell the refined products (gasoline, diesel) for more than they pay for the raw oil—and with refineries currently running at 93.5%, they're operating near full capacity to capture that margin.

The broader story fueling this move is geopolitical risk compressing supply expectations. Beyond Iran's attacks, there's talk of Ukraine targeting Russian refineries and uncertainty about U.S. intervention (Trump ruled out nukes and ground troops, leaving military options ambiguous). With tanker rates surging and the "real" cost to physically deliver oil running $30–40 higher than the headline price, the economics favor refiners who can operate at volume—which is exactly Marathon's business model.
